clues.name: Meadow Viper
clues.fact: Europe's smallest viper is also its most threatened snake, at risk from grazing, mowing, fire and illegal collecting.

clues.name: common selfheal
clues.fact: The names self-heal and heal-all come from its uses in traditional medicine, and the Quileute put its juice on boils.

clues.name: European Toad
clues.fact: Normally solitary, toads gather in large numbers at certain breeding ponds, and some are killed on roads during these annual migrations.

clues.name: Lesser Stag Beetle
clues.fact: Adults can't eat solid food, so they get by drinking tree sap and the juice of fallen fruit.

clues.name: Pearly Heath
clues.fact: Easy to recognize by the broad white band under its hindwing, it usually sits in sunny spots with its wings closed.

clues.name: Poplar Admiral
clues.fact: Skipping flowers altogether, it's drawn to the smell of carrion and dung and sips minerals from tree sap, soil and sweat.

clues.name: Mallard
clues.fact: The wild ancestor of most domestic ducks, and it's been introduced as far away as New Zealand and Australia.

clues.name: Eurasian Kestrel
clues.fact: An old name for it is windhover, from its habit of hovering in the air, and kestrels were once used to keep pigeons away.

clues.name: Eurasian Sparrowhawk
clues.fact: Females are up to 25% larger than males, one of the biggest size gaps between the sexes of any bird.

clues.name: Little Stint
clues.fact: Its numbers rise and fall with lemmings, because in poor lemming years skuas and snowy owls eat Arctic waders instead.

clues.name: Baltic Macoma
clues.fact: Buried in mud, it feeds through two narrow siphons and can live in water only a tenth as salty as the sea.

clues.name: Peppery Furrow Shell
clues.fact: Star-shaped marks on the surface give away where it's buried, and if fish nibble its siphons, they grow back in a few days.

clues.name: Mallard
clues.fact: The wild ancestor of most domestic ducks, and it's been introduced as far away as New Zealand and Australia.

clues.name: Speckled Wood
clues.fact: Northern speckled woods are bigger and darker than southern ones, with longer forewings that help them handle cooler temperatures.

clues.name: Forest Bug
clues.fact: Look for the pair of points jutting forward from its shoulders, and its legs are usually red-brown or bright orange.

clues.name: Dark Green Fritillary
clues.fact: Across the Palearctic, it ranges from Europe and Morocco through Iran, Siberia and Central Asia to China, Korea and Japan.

clues.name: July Highflyer Moth
clues.fact: The July highflyer lives in the Holarctic, the northern regions of both the Old World and the New World.

clues.name: Mountain Bumble Bee
clues.fact: It nests underground in abandoned small-mammal burrows, and its colonies are small, often with fewer than 50 workers.

clues.name: Mallard
clues.fact: The wild ancestor of most domestic ducks, and it's been introduced as far away as New Zealand and Australia.

clues.name: Common Merganser
clues.fact: Groups often fish together by forming a semicircle and driving fish into shallow water, where they're easier to catch.

clues.name: Reed Bunting
clues.fact: Males have a black head and throat set off by a white neck collar, while females are much duller with streaked brown heads.

clues.name: Pine Grosbeak
clues.fact: In poor fruit years it can move long distances south or downslope looking for food, and in winter it favors small fruits like rowan.

clues.name: Slaty-backed Gull
clues.fact: Its wings show a 'string of pearls', large white crescents on the flight feathers that join a broad white trailing edge.

clues.name: Chestnut-cheeked Starling
clues.fact: It breeds in Japan, Sakhalin and the Kuril Islands, then heads south to spend winter in Taiwan, the Philippines and northern Borneo.

clues.name: Seven-spotted Lady Beetle
clues.fact: Short of aphids, it survives on pollen, nectar, thrips and whitefly, but it can't reproduce in the meantime.

clues.name: Little Egret
clues.fact: Hunted out of northwestern Europe for hat plumes in the 1800s, it's now breeding again in Britain, Ireland, France and the Netherlands.

clues.name: Green Sea Turtle
clues.fact: The green in its name comes from the fat under its shell, colored by a seagrass diet, while the shell itself is olive to black.

clues.name: Great Mormon
clues.fact: Females come in many forms, a lot of them mimics of unpalatable butterflies, and it's been studied extensively for the genetics of that mimicry.

clues.name: Lagoon Triggerfish
clues.fact: Mothers guard the eggs for 12 to 14 hours, fanning them with their fins and removing intruding starfish by mouth.

clues.name: Stripey
clues.fact: Juveniles are often seen in tide pools, and adults turn up around man-made spots like jetties and harbour walls.

clues.name: Green Anole
clues.fact: Its ancestors crossed the sea from Cuba to the southern United States, a rare case of an island lizard colonizing a mainland.

clues.name: scarlet pimpernel
clues.fact: Its flowers open only in sunshine and close when it clouds over, which earned it names like shepherd's weather glass.

clues.name: Humpback Whale
clues.fact: Its flippers are each about a third of its body length, and it usually uses bubbles to catch krill and small fish.

clues.name: Warbling White-eye
clues.fact: In Japan it's called mejiro, meaning "white eye," and it shows up often in Japanese art and was once kept as a cage bird.

clues.name: Wedge-tailed Shearwater
clues.fact: Pairs bond for several years, though a breeding season that ends in failure can lead to divorce.

clues.name: Whitebar Surgeonfish
clues.fact: A dark-edged whitish band runs from its dorsal fin across the gill cover, and it grazes algae in small groups among surge-zone boulders.

rounds.name: Kakadu National Park
rounds.official: Kakadu National Park World Heritage Site, NT, AU

clues.name: Great Egret
clues.fact: It nests in tree colonies close to water, and lately it's been spreading into more northern parts of Europe.

clues.name: Little Egret
clues.fact: Hunted out of northwestern Europe for hat plumes in the 1800s, it's now breeding again in Britain, Ireland, France and the Netherlands.

clues.name: Domestic Horse
clues.fact: Horses usually live 25 to 30 years, but Old Billy, a 19th-century horse, made it to 62, the oldest verifiable record.

clues.name: Blue Pansy
clues.fact: Its looks depend on temperature, since cold-shocked caterpillars grow into adults with fewer eyespots and heat-shocked pupae come out less blue.

clues.name: Plumed Egret
clues.fact: In breeding season it grows long, frilly white plumes on its breast and shoulders, and its bill turns red or orange.

clues.name: Rose-crowned Fruit Dove
clues.fact: Its pinkish-red crown has a yellow border, set off by a grey head and breast and an orange belly.

clues.name: Domestic Cat
clues.fact: Of an estimated 600 million domestic cats worldwide, 400 million live in Asia, including 58 million in China.

clues.name: Buff-tailed Bumble Bee
clues.fact: Used for greenhouse pollination, it's escaped and become invasive in places like Japan, Chile, Argentina and Tasmania.

clues.name: Laughing Kookaburra
clues.fact: Its laughing territorial call, often given by several birds at once, is widely used as a stock jungle sound effect.

clues.name: Gray Shrikethrush
clues.fact: One of Australasia's best-loved songbirds, it's common over most of Australia but missing from the driest inland deserts.

clues.name: Rufous-bellied Pademelon
clues.fact: It's been reported standing upright to yank up clumps of grass and throw them against its chest, possibly as a signal.

clues.name: Yellow-throated Honeyeater
clues.fact: Endemic to Tasmania, it collects hair for its nest straight from live animals, including horses, dogs and people.

rounds.official: Great Otway National Park, VIC AU

clues.name: Small White
clues.fact: Accidentally introduced to Quebec around 1860, it spread rapidly across North America, and its caterpillar is a pest of cabbage, kale and broccoli.

clues.name: Laughing Kookaburra
clues.fact: Its laughing territorial call, often given by several birds at once, is widely used as a stock jungle sound effect.

clues.name: Gray Shrikethrush
clues.fact: One of Australasia's best-loved songbirds, it's common over most of Australia but missing from the driest inland deserts.

clues.name: Jack Jumper Ant
clues.fact: Known for jumping long distances, this ant has just one pair of chromosomes.

clues.name: Blue-winged Parrot
clues.fact: It's one of only three parrots that migrate over the sea every year, with many breeding in Tasmania and wintering on the mainland.
